title: Performance optimization of an IoT‐enabled vibratory double‐slope solar still with carbon aerogel‐impregnated carbon fiber felt and phase change material
content:
Abstract

Freshwater scarcity and the low productivity of conventional solar stills create a need for improved desalination systems that enhance freshwater production while enabling continuous monitoring. To address this limitation, an IoT-enabled vibratory double-slope solar still integrating carbon aerogel-impregnated carbon fiber felt (CA-CFF), phase change material (PCM), and vibration-assisted heat transfer was developed and experimentally investigated. The IoT system enables real-time monitoring of key thermal and operating parameters during desalination. The novelty lies in the combined integration of CA-CFF for photothermal evaporation, PCM for thermal energy storage, vibration for enhanced water mixing and heat transfer, and IoT-based monitoring within a single double-slope solar still, together with systematic multi-parameter optimization. Four operating parameters, namely vibration amplitude (0.25–1.00 mm), vibration frequency (10–25 Hz), PCM mass (0.5–2.0 kg), and basin water depth (10–40 mm), were optimized using a Taguchi L16 orthogonal array. ANOVA and multiple linear regression were used to evaluate parameter significance and predict performance. The optimum combination was A4–B3–C4–D1: 1.00 mm amplitude, 20 Hz frequency, 2.0 kg PCM, and 10 mm water depth. The experimental freshwater productivity reached 5600 mL/m2/day, compared with 5647.7 mL/m2/day predicted by the Taguchi mean-response method and 5625.1 mL/m2/day by regression, with prediction errors below 1%. Maximum basin water and glass temperatures reached 69.8 and 54.1°C, respectively. The proposed system demonstrates potential for decentralized solar desalination with real-time monitoring and optimized operation.
